reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Forsage as an earning opportunity, claims that participants earn thousands of lakhs per day, and directs viewers to a WhatsApp group for further engagement. The speaker presents the platform and its registration page as a way to make money without providing a substantive risk discussion or balanced explanation of how the claimed earnings are generated.

citations.quote: here people earn thousands of lakhs per day
So I have given the link of my whatsapp group in the description

opening.argument: The available wording does not promise a guaranteed or risk-free return. The speaker says only that people supposedly earn large amounts and that the service has been running for years; neither statement explains a required investment, assures the viewer of success, or represents earnings as certain. The screen also presents ordinary sign-in and registration options, without a visible guarantee or assurance of safety. On this limited record, the material supports uncertainty about the claims rather than a definitive finding that viewers are being deceptively solicited.

citations.quote: here people earn thousands of lakhs per day
For it is running from the past six years

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution characterizes the earnings statement as a claim of scam-level returns, but the quoted wording does not establish that the speaker guarantees those results, that the speaker received them, or that viewers must pay money. Likewise, a WhatsApp-group link shows a contact route, not what the group offers or whether it solicits deposits. The registration screen shows access options, but it does not itself establish deceptive conduct.

citations.quote: here people earn thousands of lakhs per day
So I have given the link of my whatsapp group in the description

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The combination is still promotional: the speaker places the unusually large earnings claim next to an invitation to engage through WhatsApp, while the page labels Forsage a tool “to earn money” and offers registration. A guarantee need not be phrased as an explicit promise when the central message presents extraordinary recurring earnings without a meaningful qualification or risk explanation.

citations.quote: here people earn thousands of lakhs per day
So I have given the link of my whatsapp group in the description

opening.argument: The footage can be read as a brief presentation of how the Forsage website is organized, rather than proof that the creator is selling an investment. It shows the branded landing page, sign-in and registration controls, recent platform activity, and official-channel links. Those are interface and platform features; the supplied speech does not explain a payment procedure, instruct viewers to transfer funds, or document a completed personal profit. The content therefore remains consistent with commentary or a platform demonstration whose underlying claims require independent evaluation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the page a registration page does not prove the video is an investment solicitation. The prosecution identifies what the interface contains, but not an instruction to deposit, a demonstrated transaction, or a verified payout. A website walkthrough can display registration and activity while leaving the viewer to investigate the service independently; the supplied record does not show the missing instructional or transactional step.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The presentation is not neutral merely because it displays interface elements. The speaker introduces Forsage as a place where people earn very large amounts, says it has operated for years, tells viewers they can do likewise, and directs them to a WhatsApp group. The landing page reinforces that money-making purpose with a registration button, so the overall context is promotion rather than a detached demonstration.

So I have given the link of my whatsapp group in the description

opening.argument: Even accepting that the video promotes access to a blockchain-related service, the supplied evidence does not show the mechanisms that would make the promotion a scam. There is no stated deposit amount, no request for credentials, no guaranteed-return formula, no shown downline requirement, and no verified payout. The visible page offers sign-in and registration and displays platform activity, but those features alone do not establish how money moves or whether any claim is false. The safer reading is an ordinary service referral or promotional introduction whose safety is not proven either way.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution relies on the size of the earnings language and the WhatsApp invitation, but neither supplies the missing mechanism. The record does not identify a deposit, a required fee, a credential request, or an actual completed payout. A branded service page and an activity feed may be persuasive marketing, yet they do not by themselves prove an investment pool, lending arrangement, or deceptive return structure.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing details do not neutralize the observed promotion. The speaker links participation with earning thousands of lakhs per day, says viewers can do likewise, and directs them to an off-platform group; the page invites registration while describing itself as a tool to earn money. Those facts support promotion of participation even though the short video does not spell out every financial mechanism.
